title: Trajectory Classes: LCGA and Growth Mixture Models
text: simulate 700 cases two known trajectory classes — stable-low class declining class — genuine within-class variation intercept slope, .e. GMM-type data:
code: set.seed(2026) n     <- 700 cls   <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.4)                       # 1 = Declining (40%) icept <- ifelse(cls == 1, 6.0, 2.0) + rnorm(n, 0, 0.9) slope <- ifelse(cls == 1, -0.7, 0.05) + rnorm(n, 0, 0.25) waves <- 0:4 Y <- outer(icept, rep(1, 5)) + outer(slope, waves) +   matrix(rnorm(n * 5, 0, 0.8), n, 5) colnames(Y) <- paste0("score_t", 1:5)

title: Infidelity Behavior Patterns: LCA with Covariates
text: vignette walks Ventura-León et al. (2025), “Exploring Infidelity Behavior Patterns Sample Peruvian Young Adults: Latent Class Analysis,” using ventura_leon dataset bundled mixtureEM (?ventura_leon). Four hundred Peruvian young adults (75.3% women, mean age 25.3) answered 16 binary items Multidimensional Infidelity Inventory-S (MII-S), asking whether engaged particular unfaithful thought behavior. original study used latent class analysis (LCA) identify subgroups distinct patterns, related class membership sex, age, sexual orientation, relationship duration. reproduce class solution first, improve original covariate analysis: paper assigned respondent single likely class ran chi-square/ANOVA tests labels, ignores classification uncertainty. mixtureEM’s add_covariates() instead uses bias-corrected multinomial logistic regression (Vermunt, 2010) properly accounts . See ?ventura_leon full source license note.

what: Covariates: a stronger analysis than the original paper
title: Infidelity Behavior Patterns: LCA with Covariates
text: paper related class membership sex, age, sexual orientation, relationship duration assigning respondent single likely class (modal posterior) testing associations separate chi-square tests ANOVA — “classify--analyze” approach treats class membership observed without error, biases association estimates toward null (Bakk et al., 2014). Instead, hand chosen model add_covariates(), runs bias-adjusted three-step analysis (Vermunt, 2010) solution just inspected — measurement model re-estimated, classes shift feet: Standard errors: line records variance estimator produced intervals. default also carries uncertainty step-1 class solution step-3 coefficients (Bakk et al., 2014): treating classes observed rather estimated makes intervals narrow. See ?covariate_se. summary() also returns tables invisibly, odds ratios available data frame: Reference class 1 Fidelity (largest class). Reading odds ratios reference: Sex. Women higher odds Affective interest relative Fidelity, much lower odds Infidelity relative Fidelity — line paper’s finding “men likely belong sexual desire class women emotional interest fidelity classes.” Age. Older respondents higher odds Infidelity relative Fidelity, matching paper’s finding age significantly related class membership. Sexual orientation. One row looks like discovery paper’s classify--analyze approach missed: non-heterosexual respondents higher odds Sexual desire relative Fidelity (= 2.74, p = .022). omnibus test sexual orientation — one built ask whether covariate distinguishes pair classes — significant either (Wald chi-square = 6.40, df = 3, p = .094), matching paper’s null result. three pairwise contrasts tested, single row .05 strong evidence ; read omnibus row first, treat isolated significant contrast beside non-significant omnibus test hypothesis worth better-powered look, confirmed finding. Relationship duration. Neither approach finds significant association, consistent paper. good illustration mixtureEM applies bias correction whenever classes related external variables: “obvious” approach classifying testing valid classification (almost) perfect, rarely true practice.

title: mixtureEM 0.1.0
text: Initial release: latent class profile analysis via mixture modelling, including binary, categorical, continuous measurement models, structural models (predictors, distal outcomes), multi-step estimation BCH/ML bias corrections, complex survey designs, missing data handling, longitudinal models (fit_lta(), fit_rmlca()).
